title: This Ice Catches Fire and Holds 160 Times Its Volume in Gas

scenes.text: There's ice on the ocean floor that you can set on fire.
It's called methane hydrate: water molecules locked in a cage around methane gas.
Light it, and the flame keeps burning while the ice melts away.
One cubic foot of it can release about one hundred sixty cubic feet of gas.
It forms under high pressure, deep in the ocean and in frozen ground.

description:
Methane hydrate looks like ice, but warm it up and it releases enough methane to burn.
One volume of it can release up to about 160 times that volume in gas, and it forms deep in the ocean and in frozen ground.
Would you have believed ice could burn?
first_comment: Bonus: some hydrate deposits sit under the Arctic permafrost too. Would you light one?
